verdict.rationale: Wally's integrations docs say a single command points a tool at a model and starts it with no manual configuration. The `opencode` flag documentation shows that a third-party coding agent defaults to a model on this machine unless `--cloud` is passed, and the same CLI runs local models offline. However, only one agent (opencode) is evidenced, there is no list of supported popular agent CLIs, and nothing independent confirms the launch flow works. missing for 10: documentation of multiple popular third-party coding agent CLIs beyond opencode, an explicit list of supported integrations with their exact launch commands, independent or hands-on corroboration of the one-command local-model launch.

support.subject: As a developer, I can launch popular third-party coding agent CLIs pre-configured to use my local models with a single command

citations.quote: One command points a tool at a model and starts it. There is nothing to configure by hand
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
When a small model on your own machine is enough, the same CLI runs it, offline and without an account.
